story.what_it_does: Elecon makes industrial gearboxes (Gear division) and material handling equipment (MHE division), selling to domestic and overseas customers such as steel and other heavy industries. In FY2025-26 it had consolidated revenue of ₹2,366 crore and EBITDA of ₹523 crore (22.1% margin).
story.plans: Management has a ₹400 crore capex plan for FY26-FY28 and targets ₹5,000 crore revenue and a 50% international revenue share by FY30. For H2 FY27 it guided to mid-double-digit growth of about 15%.
story.moat: The notes cite about 40% share of the domestic organised market and a reputation in heavy-duty gearboxes, though no formal moat is described. Competitors with local plants and high inventory are pressuring prices on new MHE projects, and the notes show MHE has weaker pricing protection than Gear.

scenarios.story: Gear execution keeps lifting margins and the record order book of ₹1,635 crore converts into sales, with overseas growth and the 15% H2 guidance delivered. MHE project execution recovers and defence or naval orders arrive.
signals_to_watch: Open order book converting to revenue after reaching ₹1,635 crore at 30 September 2026
MHE EBIT margin returning to the 22-24% range management maintains for the rest of FY27

scenarios.story: Revenue grows at a low-to-mid double-digit pace with EBITDA margin around 21-23%, as Gear does well and MHE recovers slowly. Uncertainty over geopolitics and input costs keeps management cautious.
signals_to_watch: H2 FY27 revenue growth versus the roughly 15% guidance
Consolidated EBITDA margin versus 23.1% in Q2 FY27

scenarios.story: Delays in orders and project clearances recur, as they did in FY26, and rising input costs plus price competition squeeze margins. Gear dispatch deferrals and a weak MHE would leave guidance missed again.
signals_to_watch: MHE EBIT margin, which fell to 20.2% from 25.7% year on year in Q2 FY27
Gear EBIT margin and input-cost pressure, after the 17.9% seen in Q1 FY27
